numeric_contract.interpretation: A fixed dtype-scaled numerical screen, not a rigorous bound on all upstream autograd/GEMM accumulation errors, an economic gate, or a claim of mathematical equality.
numeric_contract.definitions: eps = finfo(original_gradient_dtype).eps; r = 32 * eps; all audit norms/dots accumulated in float64; u64 = finfo(float64).eps / 2; gamma(k) = k*u64/(1-k*u64).
numeric_contract.split_backward_tolerance: tau_sum = r * (||grad(P)_all||_2 + ||grad(A)_all||_2). Require ||grad(P+A)_all - (grad(P)_all + grad(A)_all)||_2 <= tau_sum. If the scale is zero, require exact equality.
numeric_contract.private_projection_check: Pre-clip private gradient copied from the split control must be bitwise unchanged; post-global-clip private magnitudes need not match because the common clip coefficient may change.
numeric_contract.materially_resolvable_projection: All mechanical checks pass, dot(gP,gA) < -tau_dot, and ||gA_projected-gA||_2 > tau_projection after casting back to the original dtype.
numeric_contract.numerically_indistinguishable: Projection is exactly unchanged, or its change is <= tau_projection, or the negative dot does not exceed tau_dot. This means unresolved under this prespecified screen, not proof that the real-valued gradients coincide.
numeric_contract.direction_check: Before and after the positive global clipping factor, report dot(grad(P), assembled_gradient) and dot(grad(L_allocation), assembled_gradient), for both control and candidate; include shared-only and full-parameter results. Apply the same dot-error formula using the corresponding vector dimension when interpreting a sign.
numeric_contract.no_threshold_injection: These bounds classify audit resolution only. The projection rule itself remains strict dot < 0; no angle threshold is inserted into the method.
numeric_contract.failure_rule: If split backward exceeds its fixed allowance, dtype/backend is unsupported, or the reviewer finds the bound unjustified, status is needs_numerical_review. Do not widen tolerances, reclassify the case as harmless rounding, or proceed to fitting.
numeric_contract.assembly_dtype_contract: Compute grad(P)+grad(A) in the original gradient dtype, using the same assembly order as the proposed candidate. Cast assembled vectors to float64 only for audit residuals/norms/dots. No float64 control sum that hides original-dtype assembly effects.
numeric_contract.split_shared_backward_tolerance: Additionally require ||grad(P+A)_shared - (grad(P)_shared+grad(A)_shared)||_2 <= r*(||grad(P)_shared||_2+||grad(A)_shared||_2), with sum assembled in original dtype before float64 audit. Zero shared scale requires exact equality. All24probes must pass BOTH full973 and shared154 parity; any failure is needs_numerical_review without tolerance/sample expansion.
numeric_contract.dot_bound_limit: gamma(308) concerns only float64 dot-product rounding. The2r+r^2 term is a perturbation budget assuming each vector has relative perturbation at most r; neither full nor shared split parity proves this as an upstream autograd error bound.
